correctness.rationale: The endpoint convolution norm equals the normalized absolute kernel sum. The VP kernel factorization is standard and independently reconstructed. Partitioning the nm samples into n-point cosets preserves the numerator sign; differentiating the cotangent multiplication formula gives the needed cosecant-square identity. This reduces each coset exactly to n times the absolute three-term Dirichlet kernel. The s=0 singular-looking case is verified by the continuous limit V_n(0)=3n. The residue formulas follow from summing the unique negative arc of 1+2 cos. No finite experiment is used to justify the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: De la Vallée Poussin means are a canonical Fourier summation family, and discrete Lebesgue constants govern stability of sampled approximation. The theorem gives an exact all-scale structural collapse for every n and every quotient size m>=4, rather than a one-off numerical table: a high-degree sampled kernel has precisely the stability constant of a three-frequency projection on the quotient grid. This explains a non-obvious scale invariance and converts a growing-degree endpoint norm problem into a fixed three-frequency one.
